module purpose: neorv32_uart is a bus-controlled UART that stores control settings, moves transmit bytes from the bus through a TX FIFO and serializer to uart_txd_o, samples uart_rxd_i into a receive engine and RX FIFO for later bus readout, and generates RX/TX interrupts and RTS flow-control output.

use-case flows.value: UART control settings and FIFO-clear commands written from the bus into control registers
transmit byte path from bus write data through the TX FIFO into the serializer and out on uart_txd_o
receive byte path from uart_rxd_i through synchronizing and shift-register capture into the RX FIFO
TX and RX interrupt requests, receive-overrun status, and RTS flow-control output
control/status bits and received byte returned on bus_rsp_o.data
control registers, interrupt outputs, TX/RX engines, overrun flag, and RTS output forced to known values when rstn_i='0'

conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure flow stores the enable bit in `ctrl.enable <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_en_c);` (line 179). Its value directly controls exported clock-generator enable (`clkgen_en_o <= ctrl.enable;`, line 228), TX and RX engine activation (`tx_engine.state(2) <= ctrl.enable;`, line 344, and `rx_engine.state(1) <= ctrl.enable;`, line 417), interrupt generation (lines 270 and 315), FIFO clearing (lines 259 and 304), overrun clearing (line 458), and RTS behavior (line 473), so corruption breaks implemented enable/disable behavior; the setting is also held between writes and exported on clkgen_en_o.

The configure flow stores the prescaler and baud fields in `ctrl.prsc <= bus_req_i.data(...)` (line 182) and `ctrl.baud <= bus_req_i.data(...)` (line 183). These values define the selected UART timing because `uart_clk <= clkgen_i(to_integer(unsigned(ctrl.prsc)));` (line 229), the transmitter loads `tx_engine.baudcnt <= ctrl.baud;` (lines 349 and 368), and the receiver loads `rx_engine.baudcnt <= '0' & ctrl.baud(9 downto 1);` and `<= ctrl.baud;` (lines 422 and 432); wrong values corrupt transmit and receive timing.

The configure flow stores `ctrl.hwfc_en <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_hwfc_en_c);` (line 181). This setting changes operation at two RTL-visible points: the transmitter only advances when CTS permits or hardware flow control is disabled (line 359), and the RTS output logic takes the hardware-flow-control branch only when `ctrl.hwfc_en = '1'` (lines 472-480).

The configure flow stores the RX and TX interrupt-enable bits in lines 185-189, and the read-out flow reports them in lines 208-212. The report flows depend on these settings because `irq_tx_o` is computed from `ctrl.irq_tx_empty` and `ctrl.irq_tx_nhalf` with TX FIFO status (lines 270-272), while `irq_rx_o` is computed from `ctrl.irq_rx_nempty`, `ctrl.irq_rx_half`, and `ctrl.irq_rx_full` with RX FIFO status (lines 315-318); corruption changes which FIFO conditions raise interrupts.

The control register captures clear requests in `ctrl.clr_rx <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_rx_clr_c);` (line 190) and `ctrl.clr_tx <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_tx_clr_c);` (line 191), after defaulting them to `'0'` each cycle (lines 173-174). These decisions directly affect buffered-data preservation because `tx_fifo.clear` and `rx_fifo.clear` assert when the corresponding clear bit is `'1'` (lines 259 and 304), so corruption can wrongly discard queued receive or transmit data; availability of buffered data also depends on these commands being correct.

The transmit operate flow loads the frame register with `tx_engine.sreg <= tx_fifo.rdata & '0';` (line 351), drives the current output bit with `tx_engine.txd <= tx_engine.sreg(0);` (line 365), shifts the remaining bits with `tx_engine.sreg <= '1' & tx_engine.sreg(...);` (line 370), and exports the result on `uart_txd_o <= tx_engine.txd;` (line 392). Integrity requires the serial output to follow this load/shift/output sequence; availability is implemented under the RTL-visible conditions that data is available and the timing/CTS conditions in lines 352 and 358-360 are met.

conceptual assets.concept: Received serial byte being assembled for buffering
conceptual assets.reasoning: The receive operate flow takes the serial input at `rx_engine.sync(2) <= uart_rxd_i;` (line 408), detects/starts reception at lines 424-425, and shifts sampled bits into `rx_engine.sreg <= rx_engine.sync(2) & rx_engine.sreg(...);` (line 434). The assembled byte is then presented to the RX FIFO with `rx_fifo.wdata <= rx_engine.sreg(7 downto 0);` and `rx_fifo.we <= rx_engine.done;` (lines 305-306), so correct buffering and later delivery depend on the integrity of the sampled input and shift-register contents.

The overrun report is stored by `rx_engine.over <= '1';` when `(rx_fifo.we = '1') and (rx_fifo.free = '0')` (lines 460-461), and cleared on reset or when `ctrl.enable = '0'` (lines 455-459). The read-out flow returns this flag on `bus_rsp_o.data(ctrl_rx_over_c) <= rx_engine.over;` (line 214), so correct error reporting depends on the flag latching exactly this condition; its availability is also established because the flag remains set until cleared by the implemented conditions.

The report flow registers `irq_tx_o <= ctrl.enable and ((ctrl.irq_tx_empty and (not tx_fifo.avail)) or (ctrl.irq_tx_nhalf and (not tx_fifo.half)));` (lines 270-272). Integrity requires the transmitted interrupt event to match these configured TX FIFO conditions whenever the UART is enabled; availability is implemented by recomputing the registered output on each rising edge.

The report flow registers `irq_rx_o <= ctrl.enable and ((ctrl.irq_rx_nempty and rx_fifo.avail) or (ctrl.irq_rx_half and rx_fifo.half) or (ctrl.irq_rx_full and (not rx_fifo.free)));` (lines 315-318). Integrity requires the reported RX interrupt event to follow these configured RX FIFO conditions when enabled; availability is implemented by recomputing the registered output on each rising edge.

The report/control flow drives `uart_rtsn_o` according to hardware-flow-control mode: when `ctrl.hwfc_en = '1'`, the output is forced to `'1'` if `ctrl.enable = '0'` or `rx_fifo.half = '1'`, otherwise `'0'`; when hardware flow control is disabled, the output is `'0'` (lines 472-480). Integrity requires the exported RTS decision to match these conditions exactly because it controls the peer's permission to keep sending.
